raw.body:
feat: warn at validate time on XPath versions the runtime rejects

Since ac-46638 only an explicit version xpath-10 executes; every other
schema-valid XPath declaration validated clean and then failed at run
time. validate now flags each xpath-typed criterion, Selector Object,
and replacement targetSelectorType whose declared version is not
xpath-10 with an unsupportedXpathVersion warning naming the runtime
rejection and the xpath-10 remedy; --strict promotes it to an error.
The declarations stay specification-valid metadata per the v1.1.0
5.8.12.1 table, so severity is warning, mirroring
unsupportedOperationPath.

Wording follows the document's declared version. Arazzo 1.0.x has no
xpath-31 token (4.6.12.1 allows only xpath-30/20/10) while its omitted
form still defaults to XPath 3.1 (4.6.11.3, 4.6.12), so a pre-1.1
advisory names "XML Path Language 3.1" and the 1.0.x Criterion
Expression Type Object instead of citing xpath-31 - resolving the
pre-1.1 wording observation from the ac-46638 re-review at the
validate surface.

The advisory logic lives in a new xpath_advisory module rather than in
the god-listed arazzo-validate lib.rs; lib.rs changes are limited to
the new kind, the module hook in validate_expression_type, and
threading the document version to the three declaration sites. Tests
seed the decomposition plan's single integration harness
(tests/validation.rs with cases/ submodules) instead of growing the
inline test module; a CLI test pins the --json kind and the --strict
promotion. No golden, snapshot, or conformance status changes.
